insights.claim: The production container ships no executable binaries—only static YAML data files—making FIPS compliance a base-image concern rather than an application-level one.
insights.reasoning: The Konflux Dockerfile copies only data/*.yaml files into the image and runs sleep infinity. The Go binaries are built by the Makefile but used only during CI/CD pipeline execution. This means FIPS compliance at the container level is entirely inherited from the ubi-minimal-pqc base image, and the CI/CD binaries (which use CGO_ENABLED=0) operate outside the FIPS boundary.

insights.claim: The component follows a data-sidecar pattern where build-time tools generate static catalogs that are packaged into a volume-mountable container, decoupling metadata collection from runtime serving.
insights.reasoning: The model-extractor runs during CI/CD to fetch and assemble YAML catalogs. The production image packages these static files and exposes them as volumes. Platform components mount these volumes to consume catalog data. This architectural separation means the container has no runtime dependencies, no network requirements, and no failure modes beyond the data being stale.

insights.claim: CI/CD authentication tokens (HF_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN) are optional environment variables with no rotation or secret management integration documented in the repository.
insights.reasoning: Both tokens are read from environment variables via os.Getenv with no expiry checking, secret store integration, or rotation mechanism. While this is standard for CI/CD pipelines where secrets are injected by the CI system, the absence of any documented secret management means token handling relies entirely on external CI configuration.
